title: Adaptive invocation log sanitizer and span-key indexer
author: Maya Kline
release_notes: Adds a privacy-aware log sanitizer, token-weighted sampling for traces, and a span-key indexer + new dashboard panels for per-invocation cost/latency breakdowns. No customer-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: We are seeing two recurring problems in production telemetry: (1) invocation logs frequently contain high-cardinality or sensitive fields that increase storage cost and complicate searches, and (2) rare long-tail invocations contribute disproportionate token cost noise which destabilizes alerting and SLOs. This PR introduces an adaptive, tenant-aware log sanitizer and a span-key indexer that together reduce telemetry cardinality, protect PII, and enable fast lookups for heavy-cost invocations. Design summary: - LogSanitizer: a pipeline stage that applies tenant-configurable masking rules (regex + allowlist), numeric bucketing for high-cardinality IDs, and an optional stable signature hash for invocation identity (salted per-tenant with rotation support). The sanitizer emits metrics (sanitizer.masked, sanitizer.dropped, sanitizer.signature_assigned) to track effectiveness. - Token-weighted reservoir sampler: a lightweight sampler that prefers sampling invocations with higher estimated token-cost (configurable weight function). This keeps a small, high-signal trace corpus for debugging cost/quality regressions without exploding storage. Emits sampler.token_weight_total and sampler.sampled_count. - SpanKeyIndexer: a compact index of synthesized span keys (stable low-cardinality identifiers derived from span edge patterns). Implemented as an LSM-backed shard with bloom-filter quick checks, optimized for append-heavy workloads and low-memory tail. Exposes a query API for the Invocation Explorer dashboard. - Dashboard + alerts: new dashboard (Observability / Invocation Explorer) with panels for per-invocation token cost breakdown, model-stage latency waterfall, and sampled trace links. Alert tuning changes: the token-cost spike alert now uses a decayed baseline and an adaptive dampener keyed by invocation_signature to reduce noisy duplicates. Backwards compatibility: sanitizer defaults are conservative and off by default per-tenant; sampling and indexing are opt-in. Migration/rollout: gradual rollout by tenant flag with canary telemetry enabled. Checklist: - [x] core sanitizer implementation and unit tests - [x] span-key indexer and index query API - [x] token-weighted sampler + integration tests - [x] dashboard JSON + panels - [x] docs: docs/observability/adaptive-sampling.md - [x] perf bench: small load test showing <5% additional CPU at 1000 rps - [x] security review by SRE (SRE-404) Testing: local unit and integration tests, e2e with synthetic high-cardinality payloads, manual canary verification on staging for 3 tenants. Monitoring: added metrics and traced slow paths; main SLOs to watch during rollout are telemetry-ingest-latency, sanitizer.cpu_percent, sampler.sampled_rate, and spanindex.write_latency. Related: builds on earlier work in ENG-1879 around token attribution. This PR intentionally does not change public generation APIs; it focuses on server-side telemetry and observability.

review_comments: Alexei: Great work. Two nits: use sync.Pool for temporary buffers in scrubber to reduce GC pressure; and please add a knob to fully disable signature hashing per-tenant.
Maya (author): Added sync.Pool and tenant-level feature flag. Also exposed rotate_salt endpoint for ops. PTAL.
Priya: Could we add a safety limit to the span index shard size? If an attacker floods with synthetic span patterns we can OOM. Suggest shard-level eviction and a hard cap.
Maya: Added LRU-style compaction with configurable shard_max_segments; included metrics for eviction.count.
Jordan: Verified integration tests and approved. Noted one flake in e2e that was due to jitter; marked as flake and reran CI.
Alexei: Approving after addressing buffer reuse and adding documentation on privacy knobs.
Release Manager: Chose squash merge to keep history compact. Deployed to staging canaries 2/19, full rollout complete 2/22.
